Adenosine Deamination activity in CSF can be used for diagnosis of Tubercular meningitis.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a simple, rapid and cost effective test for differentiating tuberculous meningitis from other causes of aseptic meningitides.
the development and application of the ADA method for the diagnosis of tubercular meningitis.
the estimation of ADA level in CSF in various types of meningitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ADA estimation in T.B. Meningitis is a simple, inexpensive and fairly specific test for the diagnosis of tubercular aetiologies in meningitis.
ADA estimation in the CSF of suspected TBM patients is a rapid, simple and fairly specific method of differentiating tuberculous aetiologies from other causes.
ADA level estimation is a useful and cost effective method for making a definite diagnosis of TBM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ADA estimation in the CSF of TBM is a simple, rapid and fairly specific method for differentiating the tuberculoid etiology from non tuberculoid ones.
ADA level estimation is a useful tool for the diagnosis of TUBERCULOUS Meningitis.

ADA estimation is a simple, rapid and inexpensive method of diagnosing TBM and it should be made a routine investigation for making a diagnosis in TBM, when there is a difficulty of differentiating TBM from non tubercular causes of meningitis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ADA is a very sensitive marker for TBM and can be used as a screening tool to differentiate between tubercular and non tubercular meningitis.
ADA estimation in TUBERCULOUS meningitis has a high sensitivity and specificity.
ADA estimation in T.B. meningitis has a high specificity and positive predictive value.
